title: TTL-based connection recycling + priming heuristics for cross-SDK transports
creator: Ava Martinez
description: Introduce a TTL-driven connection recycling policy and a lightweight connection priming heuristic across Python, TypeScript (Node), and Go SDKs. Goal: reduce long-lived silent connections that cause head-of-line stalls or degraded throughput while keeping warm-connection latency low for bursty request patterns.
acceptance_criteria: SDK defaults provide a TTL (connection_max_age) that can be tuned per-client and is documented
Priming heuristic enables a single lightweight priming request after idle > threshold without creating multiple simultaneous priming requests
End-to-end test harness demonstrates 10-25% latency P95 improvement for mixed burst workloads compared to current baseline without increasing 99th percentile error rate
Telemetry emitted: connection_recycle_trigger, priming_started, priming_succeeded/failed, recycle_reason (ttl|idle|error)
Migration docs for existing customers and changelog entry included
risks: Aggressive TTL may increase connection churn and slightly raise short-term egress/connect costs
Priming requests add additional upstream load which may affect rate-limited backends if not scoped correctly
Language-level differences (Go reuse semantics vs Node Agent vs Python httpx) require slightly different config knobs and careful docs to avoid confusion
design_notes: We prefer a soft TTL (connection_max_age) with jittered expiration to avoid thundering reconnects across many clients

Priming will be a single non-streaming HEAD or OPTIONS-level request by default (configurable). For streaming-only routes, priming should warm the TLS + TCP + HTTP/2 connection but not start heavy upstream work
Expose simple per-client config: connection_max_age_seconds, idle_recycle_seconds, priming_after_idle_seconds, priming_request_method (HEAD|OPTIONS|GET)
language_specific_guidance: Python: default to using httpx.AsyncClient with limits=PoolLimits(max_keepalive_connections=16, max_connections=64) and set connection_max_age_seconds=300. Implement priming via client.get('/_priming_ping') with timeout=250ms

TypeScript (Node): recommend node: http.Agent (keepAlive:true) with keepAliveMsecs=10000 and an SDK wrapper controlling maxSockets and maxFreeSockets. Add Agent-level connection_max_age and implement priming by issuing a HEAD to /_ping with agentOptions.timeout=200

Go: net/http Transport with IdleConnTimeout=90s, MaxIdleConnsPerHost=100, and a recycle controller that removes a connection after connection_max_age_seconds. Priming should use a lightweight Request with context timeout=150ms
implementation_notes: Add a small background goroutine / async task per client that checks connection ages and triggers orderly close of oldest idle connections when TTL elapsed
Priming must be rate-limited per-client: backoff multipliers (1s, 2s, 4s) for failed priming to avoid hot loops
Mark priming as opt-out for enterprise customers worried about extra upstream calls (config: priming.enabled=false)
testing_notes: Create a synthetic load harness: bursty arrival process (Poisson + periodic spikes) and measure P50/P95/P99 and tokens/sec under persistent vs TTL-recycle scenarios
Unit tests for configurable jitter on TTL expiry and for ensuring only one concurrent priming attempt per client
Chaos tests: short TTL + upstream slow-accept to see reconnect storm behavior; assert backoff prevents cascading failures
telemetry_requirements: Emit connection_ttl_seconds when a connection is recycled
Emit priming_attempt and priming_result metric with labels: lang, client_id, route
Tag existing latency spans with connection_reused=true/false to correlate priming effect
migration_and_docs: Write migration guide: why TTL defaults chosen, how to tune for low-latency vs cost, examples for python/ts/go
Changelog entry: 'SDK: added per-client connection_max_age and optional priming heuristic to reduce head-of-line latency under bursty load'
Add recommended presets: 'low-latency', 'balanced', 'cost-saving' with explicit numeric settings
next_steps: Finalize API shapes for SDKs (PR reviews in progress)
Add telemetry hooks and validate in staging for 48h
Roll out default settings behind a feature flag for 10% of prod traffic and monitor errors/latency
